To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) endurance sled dogs have unique metabolic and dietary energy requirements; (2) these requirements can vary with load pulled, terrain, temperature and other variables; (3) these requirements are higher than previously thought; (4) the carbohydrate content of these diets also suggests that presumed fat intake may be slightly less; and (5) these findings have important implications for the nutritional management of these dogs.
the energy requirements of endurance sled dogs vary with load pulled, terrain, ambient temperature and activity.

(i) the energy expenditure of endurance sled dogs is greater than previously estimated, (ii) the energy expenditure is influenced by the terrain and load pulled, (iii) the dietary carbohydrate contents of these sled dogs are similar to those of other working dogs, (iv) the dietary fat contents are slightly lower than previous reports and (v) these data support previous findings that the energy requirements of endurance sled dogs vary substantially with environmental factors.
